claims: As of late March 2026, U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages are approaching 6.5%–7% in many cases.
As of late March 2026, U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages are near a six-month high.
The U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average climbed from around 6.22% to 6.38% or higher.
Some lenders are quoting U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages above 6.6%.
For the week of March 26-29, 2026, the National Average 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate is ~6.38% - 6.64%.
For the week of March 26-29, 2026, the National Average 15-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate is ~5.75% - 6.03%.
For the week of March 26-29, 2026, the National Average 5/1 ARM Mortgage Rate is ~6.56% - 7.40%.
Last week, 30-year refinance rates rose from 6.72% to 6.97%.
U.S. mortgage rates are following the 10-year Treasury yield.
Some forecasts from early March suggested rates could settle near 6.1% to 6.3% later in 2026.
In South Korea, 30-year fixed rates have crossed the 7% threshold for the first time in over a year.
